    Grimmel Civic Guard¶

    [!INFO] The Plow and the Bell — Citizens Who Muster Grimmel has no standing army by law — and the best militia in the south by habit.

    History¶

    The Grimmel Civic Guard is not an order and insists on the point. The Grimmel Republic — founded by settlers who fled both Erisian Empire and Erisian church in the Erisian expansion to build a state too small to oppress and too weak to crusade — forbids a standing army by the Assembly's founding compact. What it has instead is a citizen-militia that musters only when the bell rings, and has rung often enough to become tradition.

    Every landholding adult in the Republic is technically a guardsman; practically, the Guard is the farmers, craftsmen, and town clerks who train one day in seven and know every ravine and cave system of Grimmel's rolling farmland and wooded groves. Geography has been Grimmel's ally: between the Limese League and the Vennerian Trade Republic, any invader must cross a power that finds Grimmel more useful as buffer than as prize — a buffer the Guard makes expensive to ignore.

    In 596 AGD the Black Agent — carrying the encoded consciousnesses of Mana Mortvagn's lineage — drifted to Grimmel's coast, drawn by the unusually dense mage-cells of the Eisenheart and Mortvagn families. A year later Emrys and Ichi were born to the Eisenhearts; Lucien Mortvagn to the Mortvagns — with Mana Mortvagn to follow. The Guard, unknowing, posted extra watches that winter because something felt watched; the Assembly minutes record it as weather.

    Patron¶

    The Citizens' Assembly and the elected First Citizen (single five-year term). The Guard swears not to a crown or saint but to the bell — the civic bell of Grimmel town, whose rope any citizen may pull. Chaplains are not appointed; any faith may bless a muster, and the Guard has been blessed by Erisian priests, Elven-nature celebrants, and once, memorably, by an Ironcloak preceptor who told them they were already Ironcloak and left before anyone could arrest him. The Assembly apologized to the Pontificate of Eris and kept his pamphlet.

    Sigil¶

    A green sheaf of grain crossed with a wooden bell-clapper on a cream field, bordered in Grimmel's civic blue when fielded formally. No crown, no cross, no stag. Companies add a small Silver Bride-silver disc behind the sheaf when they march at night — not mysticism but practical: polished silver reflects the ring's light well enough to rally by.

    Role¶

    Territorial militia, disaster response, and buffer defense. The Guard does not project force — it denies it to others: holding passes, flooding fords, and disappearing into cave systems where, local rumor insists, relics of the Glorious Alliance crash still wait. Its competence is homely and real: logistics by farm wagon, surgery by traveling healer-mages who can close a cut before it poisons, and a habit of winning not battles but weeks — enough for Venner or Limese to decide intervention is cheaper than conquest.

    The two magical families are its quiet edge: the Eisenhearts and Mortvagns produce youths whose mage-cell density can, under stress, act as beacons or shields — effects the Guard attributes to luck.

    Relation to Currencies & Regions¶

    The Guard pays no wages — service is civic duty — but the Assembly's war chest is Erilia and grain. Grimmel exports grain and imports manufactured goods; its market at Grimmel town is where Anosi Mark counting plates from the Anos Plutocracy quarter convert to Erilia at rates the Guard's clerks publish on the bell-house wall to shame gougers. Small Meblean Pearl hoops from Sousu circulate as prestige savings (a Grimmel dowry pearl is a Pearl that stayed).

    When Vennerian Ducat prices spike at Beast's Bay, Grimmel feels it as bread prices months later — the Guard's real war is always against that delay.
